Let \(p=\ell=2r+1\). Since \(r\) is an odd prime, \(p\equiv 3\pmod 4\), so
\[
\chi(-1)=-1.
\]
Also, since \(2\) generates \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), it is not a square, hence
\[
\chi(2)=-1.
\]
This also forces \(p\equiv 3\pmod 8\), so \(r\equiv 1\pmod 4\).

For \(x\in H\setminus\{1\}\), neither \(1+x\) nor \(1-x\) is zero, so
\[
N_{\varepsilon,\delta}
=\frac14\sum_{x\in H\setminus\{1\}}
(1+\varepsilon\chi(1+x))(1+\delta\chi(1-x)).
\]
Thus we need
\[
A=\sum_{x\in H\setminus\{1\}}\chi(1+x),\quad
B=\sum_{x\in H\setminus\{1\}}\chi(1-x),\quad
C=\sum_{x\in H\setminus\{1\}}\chi(1-x^2).
\]

Use the standard quadratic character sum
\[
J=\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p}\chi(t)\chi(1-t)=1
\]
for \(p\equiv3\pmod4\). Then
\[
B=\frac12\sum_{x\ne0}(1+\chi(x))\chi(1-x)
=\frac12(-1+J)=0.
\]
Similarly,
\[
\sum_{x\in H}\chi(1+x)
=\frac12\sum_{x\ne0}(1+\chi(x))\chi(1+x)
=\frac12(-1-1)=-1,
\]
so
\[
A=-1-\chi(2)=0.
\]

Finally, pair \(x\) with \(x^{-1}\) in \(H\setminus\{1\}\). There are no fixed points, and
\[
\chi(1-x^{-2})
=\chi\!\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x^2}\right)
=\chi(-(1-x^2))
=-\chi(1-x^2),
\]
so \(C=0\).

Therefore
\[
N_{\varepsilon,\delta}
=\frac14(r-1)
\]
for every \((\varepsilon,\delta)\in\{\pm1\}^2\).

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{r-1}{4},\frac{r-1}{4},\frac{r-1}{4},\frac{r-1}{4}\right)}
\]
